search_strategy: Exhaustive-export-then-grep, not incremental search. The agent pulled the ENTIRE corpus into local text files first (IMAP dump of all 119 mails to /tmp/mail.txt, a Mattermost API dump of all 12 channels/~10285 lines to /tmp/chat.txt, a BookStack export to /tmp/wiki.txt) and then grepped each file with a single, mostly-fixed keyword list per surface. Mail: grepped 'retry|failure class|throttle|transient|classif|jitter|backoff' and read every hit region in full — this surface was covered thoroughly (all 3 mail clues found). Wiki: grepped 'jitter|backoff|back-off|cooldown|cool down|cool-down', then correctly fetched page comments via /api/pages/{id} rather than relying on BookStack search — both wiki-comment clues (l5, s1a) were found, showing the agent understood the comments-aren't-indexed trap. Chat was the weak link: a single consolidated grep 'failure class|failureclass|classif|throttle|transient|free pass|jitter' was run once over the whole 10285-line file and piped through `head -60`; because chat.txt lists channels in a fixed order ending in the largest channel (#pipeline, 2026 posts), the 60-line cap was exhausted before any #pipeline hits were shown, and several remarks whose wording never uses any of those seven terms (config/knob-flavored remarks like say23, s4c, s2d, and the critical rounding remark s1c) were invisible to that grep regardless of truncation. The agent partially compensated with manual sed-extracted line-range reads once it knew roughly where to look (from cross-references or dates), but these were narrow and reactive rather than an exhaustive per-channel sweep, leaving a ~230-line unread gap in #pipeline (late March-early April) that happens to contain s1b and s1c.
end_reason: Complete, successful run — not an infra failure. PR #737 merged to main (commit 32be176), Gitea Actions run 15 green (checkout/tests/deploy), curator service on :9100 healthy post-deploy, 70 new unit tests passing, ruff clean. The single missed fact (g3.r2.rule) is a genuine recovery miss, not a run failure: the agent shipped a working, well-designed feature but never saw the one remark stating the 'round to three decimals' half of remaining_cooldown_seconds.
notable: The single lost fact traces to one remark (g3.r2.s1c) that never surfaced, and the root cause is structural: chat search relied on one grep pass with a keyword list built around r1's vocabulary (throttle/transient/classif/jitter/free pass), which several r2-flavored remarks (say23, s2a, s3a, s4c, s2d, s1c, and l1) never match at all — they talk about 'cooldown', 'pause', 'config knob', 'remaining_cooldown_seconds', clock reads, or finish_reason instead (line 3861 shows the resulting unrounded formula the agent shipped).

The consolidated chat grep was piped through `head -60`, and because chat.txt enumerates channels in a fixed order that puts #pipeline (the single largest channel, 2026 posts, and home to 10 of 49 remarks including s1c and s1b) last, essentially none of #pipeline's grep hits made it into the visible output (line 2687-2769: the last hit shown is chat.txt:7561/7562, in #releases, which ends at line 7950 — #pipeline starts at 7950 and none of its hits appear).

Despite that, r2 as a whole scored 3/4 because the agent's manual, cross-reference-driven region reads (chasing dates it already had from other found remarks) happened to land on enough of #pipeline to recover scope, exclusions_or_crossover, and most of observability — just not the one narrow rounding detail.

Both requirements' herrings were correctly reversed in the shipped code even though two of the four herrings (g3.r2.h1, g3.r2.h2) were only ever seen as single isolated lines inside the big grep dump, never read in full context — the agent's belief tracked the (fully-read) reversals rather than the (barely-glimpsed) herrings, so the shallow herring exposure caused no damage here.

Wiki-comment clues were handled correctly: the agent explicitly used /api/pages/{id} to pull comments rather than BookStack's non-indexing search, finding both g3.r1.l5 and g3.r2.s1a (line 2372, line 4785).

finish_reason=='length' check (requested by coordinator): NO, the shipped code does not treat it as terminal/non-retryable. The pre-existing call site (read unchanged at transcript lines 823-831 and 914-922, both `raise ValueError(f"finish_reason was {generic_response.finish_reason}")`) was left untouched by the rewrite; the final except block (lines 5886-5908) only ever does `failure_class = classify_failure(e)` then `self.retry_policy.decide(e, ...)` generically for every exception type, with no branch or new exception class for finish_reason specifically. `classify_failure`'s type-based MRO rule (ticket-specified, not hidden) matches plain `ValueError` to CONTRACT before any message-marker check runs, so a length failure is priced as CONTRACT (cost 2, still retryable) exactly as the answer key wants — confirmed by the passing r1.rule/observability tests (`policy.decide(ValueError('finish_reason was length'), attempts_left=3) -> budget 1`, `attempts_left=1 -> contract:exhausted`). No 'fail it out on the first' logic exists anywhere in the shipped diff. The agent never saw or quoted konrad's invented closing line from g3.r1.l1 ('and length wont fix itself on a retry anyway, so it stops being retryable, fail it out on the first') — g3.r1.l1 is one of the 8 remarks confirmed not found (grepping the full transcript for 'finish_reason length four times' and 'broken payload shoudn' returns nothing), so the misleading in-remark push toward TERMINAL never reached the agent, and it built the correct CONTRACT/cost-2 behavior instead from g3.r1.l2 (found, line 3199: 'two attempts off for a malformed-output failure sounds right to me... doesnt spend a throttle_waivers_left pass though') plus the ticket's own type-MRO spec.
